text: Refines D-0333 and D-0377 for #697: the recording heap ceiling bounds the heap the gate keeps, the most live heap any collection marks during the run, read from runtime/metrics' /gc/heap/live:bytes. The peak HeapAlloc it judged before also counts garbage the collector hasn't freed yet, which depends on when the collector runs: identical runs of the 65,536-entry late-bad Go case measured 57, 212 and 65 MiB on one machine. Locally, quiet runs kept 27 to 34 MiB and runs under CPU contention up to 65 MiB. The 192 MiB ceiling, workloads, routes, GOMAXPROCS=1, GOGC=100, no memory limit and one TLC slot are unchanged, and a run with no collection fails. At GOGC=100 garbage can grow to about the kept heap again, so the old peak held the kept heap to roughly half the ceiling. A gate that keeps a 256 or 512 MiB payload still fails, as main did at 0.5 to 1.1 GB before streaming. The peak including garbage is still reported, and TestGateRecordingKeptHeapIsStable697 repeats that case three times in the integration lane and reports the spread of both. The Python converter's additional-heap ceiling is unchanged.
